story.head: The Golden Knights’ edge in preventing dangerous shots
paras: The Sabres (8-5-3) beat Columbus 5-2 on Friday, and the Golden Knights have won two in a row. Going in, the Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Sabres sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 16th).

The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st) and have one of the league’s best penalty kills (2nd). They also keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st), so the Golden Knights have the edge over the Sabres on preventing dangerous shots. As for the Sabres, they rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd), but don't block many shots (30th). They also get their shots through better than almost anyone (3rd), and their knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot.

Jack Eichel (7 G / 16 A / 23 P in 18 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring, and Mark Stone (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 18 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, with ten points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 16 GP) isn’t far behind.
Adin Hill (6-2-0 / .895 SV% in 8 GS) is expected to start for Vegas, and Colten Ellis (3-2-0 / .891 SV% in 6 GS) for Buffalo.

The Golden Knights have been without Parker Wotherspoon since Oct 10.
Rasmus Dahlin is set to play his 600th NHL game.
Zach Benson has one goal on chances worth about 5.6 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
